title.value: LEARNING TASK DECOMPOSITION WITH ORDERED MEMORY POLICY NETWORK
title.justification: The title of the paper is directly provided at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: LEARNING TASK DECOMPOSITION WITH ORDERED MEMORY POLICY NETWORK

analysis.description: The paper proposes Ordered Memory Policy Network (OMPN) to discover subtask hierarchy by learning from demonstrations. It demonstrates that OMPN can achieve higher task decomposition performance under both unsupervised and weakly supervised settings. The experiments were conducted on Craft and Dial environments to validate its performance.

type.justification: The paper includes experiments and evaluations on various environments such as Craft and Dial to demonstrate the performance of the proposed Ordered Memory Policy Network (OMPN).
type.quote: Experiments on Craft and Dial demonstrate that our model can achieve higher task decomposition performance under both unsupervised and weakly supervised settings.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on task decomposition for learning from demonstration, which falls under the reinforcement learning paradigm.
name.quote: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) a popular paradigm for policy learning and has served as a warm-up stage in many successful reinforcement learning applications.

name.justification: The paper focuses on decomposing tasks into hierarchical subtasks, which aligns with the field of hierarchical imitation learning.
name.quote: This question of discovering a meaningful segmentation of the demonstration trajectory is the key focus of Hierarchical Imitation Learning.

name.justification: The paper discusses learning from demonstration as an approach to extract useful subtask structures for policy learning.
name.quote: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) is a popular paradigm for policy learning and has served as a warm-up stage in many successful reinforcement learning applications.

name.justification: The paper introduces OMPN as the primary model to achieve task decomposition by learning from demonstration.
name.quote: In this paper, we propose a novel perspective to solve this challenge: could we design a smarter neural network architecture, so that the sub-task structure can emerge during imitation learning?
